strategy_title: maxnreg Register Cap Causes Severe Spill Regression
strategy_description: Capping registers via maxnreg (255→128) successfully doubled theoretical occupancy (12.5%→25%) and raised Block Limit Registers from 2 to 4, but achieved occupancy remained flat (11.67%→11.49%) while kernel duration increased 4.3x (39→169 µs). The register cap forced aggressive spilling to local memory, causing a new CPIStall bottleneck where warps spent 11.6 cycles stalled on L1TEX scoreboard dependencies (69% of all stall cycles), and No-Eligible warp cycles worsened from 65% to 89%. The anti-pattern is: when a large GEMM tile (128×128 FP32) already saturates registers, forcing spill via maxnreg trades register pressure for local-memory traffic that is far more expensive than the latency-hiding benefit of the marginal occupancy gain.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: no autotune, 255 registers/thread, 12.5% occupancy, 39us
@triton.jit
def kernel(A, B, out):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 128
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 128
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
    for k in range(K // BLOCK_K):
        a = tl.load(A + ...)
        b = tl.load(B + ...)
        acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
    tl.store(out + ..., acc)
applicable_when: Never: this strategy is a confirmed anti-pattern for large GEMM tiles. Do not apply maxnreg to kernels with 128x128+ FP32 accumulator tiles where register pressure is already at hardware maximum.
do_not_apply_when: Any kernel with a large accumulator tile (BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N ≥ 64×64 in FP32) where registers_per_thread is near the hardware maximum (≥200). Forcing maxnreg in this regime causes register spilling to local memory, introducing L1TEX scoreboard stalls that far outweigh any occupancy benefit. The achieved occupancy does not improve even when theoretical occupancy doubles, because the spill traffic creates new stalls that keep warps ineligible.
framework_notes: In Triton, maxnreg is passed as a parameter to triton.Config(). On Hopper (H200/H100), the hardware maximum is 255 registers/thread. Setting maxnreg=128 halves register budget and forces the compiler to spill the 128×128 FP32 accumulator (16384 elements) to local memory, creating strided L1TEX accesses with 1/32 byte sector utilization.

This caps Block Limit Registers at 2 blocks/SM, yielding only 12.5% theoretical occupancy. With 245 CTAs on 132 SMs (0.93 waves), most SMs are idle after the first wave, and 65% of scheduler cycles have no eligible warp. Reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 halves the accumulator to 64x128=8,192 elements, which should cut register pressure enough to allow 4 blocks/SM (25% theoretical occupancy) and doubles the grid to 490 CTAs (1.86 waves). The fix is to reduce BLOCK_M while preserving ALL load/store index expressions verbatim.
